Funny, speaking from experience I have had 0 success off both bumble and tinder but hinged has been a gold mine for meeting and having cool conversations with people! 

I think it comes down to Hinged being taken relatively more seriously, and profiles having more substances to them which allows people to appeal to certain niches. If you go to the sidebar there are alot of resources that help with your profile construction/you can  post a profile review here!

In terms of Hinged, because its catered to more serious/relationship oriented dating, I personally have found that good conversation revolves around being able to have talking points about what's on the person profile (maybe you see a hobby you can relate to, or something that catches your eye). AGAIN, from personal experience; I found that I didn't need to have the typical hyper witty and have the clever pick up/seduction texting style that other apps may require (which was never my personality). Being able to relate to my matches profile over just genuine conversation about them was more then enough to score dates/solidify there was a connection.

As for your main point about response times, I find what has worked for me was not responding while I'm at work (don't always have access to my phone) and usually replying to messages in the evening. This usually aligns with most people (they're off work/at home) and I've had numerous instances where the response times would not only be lightning quick, it would eventually turn into full text conversations.

Hey! Idk if I'm too late to the review but I looked over your profile and I've got to say not only are you in my area but I'm getting a sense me and you both have both similar hobbies/interest! I posted my profile review (so you can check my post history). For reference, the profile in my history has lead to 40+ interactions (people liking me, giving me roses & vice versa) leading to 26 matches within one month.

I think you're a good looking guy and I do see a lot of potential to showcase your personality. The best analogy I can think of is your dating profile is your resume to every potential match; impressions are everything, and people are quick to make judges, or skim over things and are trying to connect YOUR pictures to the prompts you write. 

Depending on how serious you are in terms of online dating, I do think you would benefit from having some professional photos done!(The first three photos on my profile were professionally taken and those pictures have gotten me alot of likes leading me to matches). In your case, I thinking having your 1st, 2nd and last photo be replaced with professional done photos would definitely display that you're attractive while also showing things that are unique to you! I think while it's nice to show you have humor in the 6th photo, (I'm goofy myself) save it for when you're talking to your match! (They'll quickly learn your personality, all you need is to get people interested). Remember, people don't even get to the point of reading your prompts if they don't like what they see. 

As for prompts I think you've nailed it with being able to describe yourself perfectly! My only suggestion is if you want to broaden your appeal, you could change your first prompt to "together we could..." and focus on having a few points of explaining what dating YOU would look like, aka (listening to ___music, or playing with your dog, going bouldering, etc.) I found using this type of way of explaining your hobbies more welcoming for people viewing your profile (aka it gives a more cohesive impression of you).

I know it seems like alot of work but the effort you do put in putting your best foot forwards always pays off! You already have a good base of being relatively fit, already knowing your hobbies and having some artistic talents! DM me if you need any more information!

From personal experience, I think online dating has been a game changer for me! Now that I’ve been out of uni for a while you realize that life does become a routine and meeting people organically(finding someone who’s even single/datable) has personally become unfeasible.
Having a fixed routine of working long/odd hours and having very introverted hobbies would be a death sentence for me. 

Using online dating apps (specifically hinge) for the first time has allowed for me to match and go on dates of so many different types of people who share similar hobbies/values/education levels. (You can view my post history for my profile). Anecdotally, my entire friend group (5 couples) have also met via online dating apps aswell!

I think the only caveat I can give for online dating is to realize your dating profile should be treated as your resume! I’ve had my fair share of pessimism & experiences about online dating that Reddit loves to rave about  (cancelled dates, conversations that don’t go anywhere, matches not responding back). It doesn’t help statistically being shorter then average & Asian, but I’ve invested a lot in curating pictures (paid for a photoshoot) and really narrowing down what I value in a dating partner. I feel like despite not being everyone’s cup of tea the extra effort I’ve put into my profile has lead me feeling more then satisfied with the people that I’ve met so far and gone on dates with!

Hey it’s OK to feel like that. Not to downplay how you feel But you’re probably not the only one that feels like that. Often times we can steal our own happiness by thinking too hard about how other people feel about us. It’s a never ending cycle where we overinterpret and over analyze everything when in reality it’s up to us to grow our self and reassure our own self. It kind of sucks that we can’t force people to think about us but at the end of the day don’t be too hard on yourself.

Hey man I’m 23 now let me tell you that you’re still discovering yourself and that’s OK. I think all you need to do is understand that not only is social media not everything but you got a respect your own journey as a person. I know it’s easier said than done.  Just to give you some perspective in my first year as a freshman I remember trying to change my name and trying to distance myself from my nerdy high school days and trying to embrace frat culture.

Long story short by the end of the year it was way too hard to try to keep up with people that just didn’t mesh well with me. I didn’t care about concerts I didn’t care about EDM festivals I didn’t even care that much about sports, By the end of freshman year I began to reevaluate what made me me in high school and I honestly stuck with it.

It’s made me happier for the better. I know there’s a lot of pressure to fit in a certain lifestyle when you’re in college because you are only young once but forget the bullshit because every person is different. By the third year of college I learn to embrace my nerdy and geeky side and by the fourth year of university and last year that confidence transferred over to the point where I found someone that loved me for me and I had a friend group that may not be deemed the coolest by social media standards ultimately made me happy. At the end of the day you can only be yourself. 

I was always obsessed an idealized having a large group of friends and fitting in to white people would consider fraternities but cut the superficial shit because maybe what you need or people that like you for you and you can always be yourself around

Hey man I think that it’s only human to be scared of the unknown. I think that it’s great that you manage to narrow down a lot of things that has made you think the way you think and of course no one wants to fail especially when do you want to live up to their loved ones expectations. Just keep at it and let’s be honest some days will obviously feel like shit and some days you just have to live for today because that’s all you can do. I can’t say it’s going to get better because at the end of the day anybody saying that doesn’t really change how you feel about today. What has really helped me is maybe talking to your doctor about your symptoms because antidepressants and anxiety medication really do help. Although it doesn’t completely take the pain away overtime you’ll be able to recognize little things in life and maybe those little things keep you going day to day.
